target_moa.text: Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor; abrocitinib reversibly and selectively inhibits JAK1 by blocking the ATP binding site, and its two primary metabolites (M1 and M2) inhibit cytokines that transduce signals via JAK1-dependent pathways.

citations.quote: Abrocitinib selectively inhibits Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) by blocking the ATP binding site and its two primary metabolites (M1 and M2) inhibit cytokines which transduce their signals via JAK1-dependent pathways.

Abrocitinib is an orally bioavailable small molecule that reversibly and selectively inhibits Janus Kinase (JAK) by blocking the ATP binding site.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%) include nasopharyngitis (12.4% at 100 mg, 8.7% at 200 mg vs 7.9% placebo), nausea (6.0% at 100 mg, 14.5% at 200 mg vs 2.1% placebo), and headache (6.0% at 100 mg, 7.8% at 200 mg vs 3.5% placebo). Serious risks include serious/opportunistic infections (herpes simplex, herpes zoster, pneumonia), thrombosis, thrombocytopenia and lymphopenia.

citations.quote: The most frequent serious infections reported in clinical studies with CIBINQO for atopic dermatitis were herpes simplex, herpes zoster, and pneumonia [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)].
Treatment with CIBINQO was associated with an increased incidence of thrombocytopenia and lymphopenia [*see Adverse Reactions (6.1)*].

detail.text: Boxed warning for Serious Infections, Mortality, Malignancy, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), and Thrombosis. Patients may be at increased risk for serious infections leading to hospitalization or death (most frequent: herpes simplex, herpes zoster, pneumonia); higher rates of all-cause mortality, malignancies, MACE, and thrombosis were observed with JAK inhibitors.

citations.quote: ## **WARNING: SERIOUS INFECTIONS, MORTALITY, MALIGNANCY, MAJOR ADVERSE CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS, and THROMBOSIS**

Patients treated with CIBINQO may be at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death; The most frequent serious infections reported with CIBINQO were herpes simplex, herpes zoster, and pneumonia [see *Warnings and Precautions (5.1) and Adverse Reactions (6.1)*].
